content.v: 《 玩具总动员3 》常被公认为最优秀的影改游戏之一。作为一款素质过硬的3D平台跳跃游戏，它能让电影粉丝沉浸式融入玩具世界，这份沉浸感是绝大多数同类影改游戏都难以实现的。因此，当年体验过原版游戏的玩家，得知Digital Eclipse计划将几乎所有历代《玩具总动员》游戏移植到现代平台，且本作也在其中时，都倍感惊喜。
官方不仅让这些老游戏重新上架，还将它们打包推出。其中“复古精选集”收录了90年代至21世纪初的全部老款《玩具总动员》游戏，同时还有适配现代平台的《玩具总动员3》高清重制版。最值得一提的是，精选集与重制版支持同捆购买，不仅有数字版，还推出了实体版本。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261122/1795311318_508284_jpg_r.jpg
几十年来，影改游戏曾是行业常态。尤其是迪士尼的头部大片，几乎都会配套推出同名改编游戏。《阿拉丁》《大力士》《泰山》——这些电影上映时都同步推出了游戏，让粉丝能用另一种方式，重温大银幕上的精彩内容。
但如今这一传统几乎已经销声匿迹，背后有多重原因。想让游戏与电影同步发售已经不再现实，核心原因在于：要做出配得上大制作电影的游戏，开发周期实在太长。哪怕电影刚有初步构思，开发商就立刻启动项目，电影制作完成的速度，也会比游戏快上好几年。

正因如此，《玩具总动员3》大概是我们能见到的最后一批真正意义上的同步影改游戏，而颇具讽刺意味的是，它恰好也是最顶尖的作品之一。尤其是重制版推出后，很多人回顾这款游戏，都开始怀念电影与同名游戏同步上线的年代。但体验这款重制版时，我们不该只停留在怀旧情绪里。游戏开发商与电影公司都应该借鉴参考：当年迪士尼与雪崩工作室打造原版游戏的思路，以及Digital Eclipse制作重制版的方法，将其作为未来影改游戏的发展范本。
尽管《玩具总动员3》的游戏与电影同期发售，但游戏并非只是电影的互动复刻版。实际上，它是献给整个系列——至少是初代三部曲的一封情书，内容取材于前三部深受观众喜爱的电影。开发团队拥有很高的创作自由度，也因此打造出了自由度更高的“胡迪牛仔秀”开放区域，这即便不是游戏爆火的唯一原因，也是最核心的因素之一。
这款游戏的成功，其实并不依赖与电影同步发售——16年后推出的完整版就印证了这一点。老玩家能重温这款佳作的魅力，感受它如何在忠于电影设定的前提下，讲述独立的玩具故事;而迪士尼也拥有了一款打磨精良的新版本，不仅能在新电影上映时吸引年轻粉丝入坑，任何时候都能拿出来作为系列的入门作品。
这正是那些几乎放弃影改游戏的工作室，最需要吸取的经验：不必强求几乎不可能实现的影游同步发售。更重要的是保证游戏本身的品质，能经得起时间的考验。只要游戏素质过硬，不仅可以随时发售，日后需要时也随时能拿出来复用。时间够久的话，还能像《玩具总动员3》一样推出重制版。
我甚至不介意十年后，《玩具总动员3》能再次翻新推出重制版。或许再过两代主机，等到系列第六、七、八部电影上映时，还能给那时还未出生的玩具总动员粉丝们游玩。给胡迪牛仔秀加一块新区域，多做几个剧情任务，这总比从零开始打造一款全新游戏容易得多——而开发成本过高，正是影改游戏时代走向终结的核心症结。

我也明白，“做一款像《玩具总动员3》一样优秀的游戏就能一劳永逸”这种话说起来容易，做起来难。但问题是，现在甚至连愿意尝试的厂商都没有了。看看《王国之心4》公布《寻梦环游记》世界时玩家的热情就知道了。《寻梦环游记》即将推出续集，如果打造一款像《玩具总动员3》一样、以亡灵世界为舞台的改编游戏，哪怕不和续集同步发售，也一定会大受欢迎。遗憾的是，在我看来，《王国之心》里加入寻梦环游记的内容，已经是我们能接触到的、最接近迪士尼亡灵世界主题游戏的作品了。

content.v: Rockstar仍未确认《GTA6》的PC版发售时间，从系列过往的发售节奏来看，PC版可能要等待7到19个月不等。不过眼下已经有一款游戏填补了这份空白。
《亡命狂奔》是一款警匪题材的“犯罪沙盒”游戏，游戏内所有警察与劫匪角色均由真实玩家扮演。本作于本月初登陆Steam，对于曾开发《地球末日：生存》《霜裔》的厂商Kefir而言，本作的发售成绩相当亮眼：11月4日峰值在线人数为2.3万，短短几天后便涨到4.3万——随着《GTA6》发售日临近，这一数字还在持续飙升。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261122/1795310674_304944_jpg_r.jpg
11月15日，《亡命狂奔》的峰值同时在线人数突破50万，达到549661人。如今PC玩家只能在社交平台刷着铺天盖地的《GTA6》内容望梅止渴，这款游戏的热度依旧居高不下。
为了更直观地体现这份热度，目前它已是Steam平台在线人数第四高的游戏，足以和《CS2》《Apex英雄》这类头部大作同台竞争：
- 《反恐精英2》——120万人
诚然，《亡命狂奔》的定位更接近《GTA Online》（尤其是角色扮演玩法），而非《GTA6》的单人剧情，但它具备GTA系列的所有核心特质：银行劫案、警匪追逐、便利店抢劫，以及贯穿系列的白手起家、打造犯罪帝国的叙事线。游戏介绍中写道：“只需一周，你就能从街头小混混成长为服务器最大帮派的老大。之后你还可以重头再来——带着积累的经验、结识的盟友，用更宏大的计划夺取权力。”
纸面来看，它算得上是《GTA6》的优质替代品，尽管魅力还比不上《NotGTAV》——那款模仿贪吃蛇的恶搞小游戏，当年曾陪玩家度过等待洛圣都的漫长时光。但这款游戏存在不小的问题：开发商Kefir承认“部分美术素材”使用了AI生成，而“褒贬不一”的玩家评价更是揭露了残酷的现状：外挂泛滥，社区环境极不友好，新人根本无法正常上手。
有玩家评价道：“一半是凑合的AI粗制内容，再加上我玩CS以来见过最严重的外挂问题，根本没法玩。”
另一条评价写道：“概念很棒，全被社区毁了。警察见你戴面具就直接乱杀，劫匪也好不到哪去。两边都蹲在交易区和撤离点守株待兔，根本没法按正常玩法玩下去。”
还有玩家提醒：“你想抢的店早就被别人抢过了，刚下车就会被其他玩家一枪崩了。我想老老实实当警察，结果选警察的人太多，根本排不进去。作为新人，我只能开车瞎逛，然后回莱尼的据点——只要一减速就会被其他劫匪开车撞。”
大量玩家评价都质疑，AI的实际使用范围远不止官方披露的程度，同时还吐槽游戏网络连接差、维护时间过长，严重影响体验。Kefir已经在着手解决部分问题：新增了更醒目的举报按钮、优化服务器、限制语音聊天以整治不良言论，同时也在升级外挂检测手段，但差评依旧在源源不断地增加。
今日发布的一条玩家评价称：“我从没见过外挂这么多的游戏。服务器开服才半小时，就有人开自瞄抢银行了。服务器还没有区域限制，情况更糟。独狼玩家根本没法玩，1打2还有可能，1打3完全没胜算……游戏本身有意思，也有潜力，但外挂、蹲点、组队玩家对独狼的碾压优势，说真的，玩起来糟心远大于乐趣。就现在的状态，不值得费这个劲。”
所以，尽管眼下它算得上是免费的《GTA6》替代品，但《亡命狂奔》的实际现状，是过度使用AI、外挂泛滥，还有连《DayZ》的乱局都相形见绌的随意击杀风气。

items.title: 《GTA6》宣传的天气系统去哪了？20小时没见一滴雨

content.v: 由你来说： 有玩家发帖称，自己在《GTA6》自由模式里玩了20多个小时，一滴雨、一声雷都没见过，而R星此前承诺过“次世代天气系统”。帖子获得168.9万次查看，评论区却立刻分成两派：一派说“我第一次去安全屋就下雨了”，一派说“任务里有，任务外没有”。更有人透露，完整天气系统要到后续章节才解锁。 你遇到特殊天气了吗？
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/11/22/small_202611220912239256.png

content.v: 第三人称生存 恐怖 游戏《PSYCHO DEAD》官方发售日宣传片公开，游戏将于2027年4月15日发售，登陆PC Steam和PS5平台，支持中文。
在玩家《PSYCHO DEAD》中，玩家将扮演一名拥有超能力的少女，在致命追猎者的追杀下，设法逃离一座秘密实验室。试玩DEMO已在Steam商店页开放。
这是一款第三人称生存恐怖游戏。故事围绕一名拥有超能力的少女展开，她试图逃离一座充斥着畸形怪物与恐怖生物的秘密实验室。揭开事件背后的真相，踏上一段惊心动魄的冒险之旅，让你始终屏息以待。探索一个充满谜团与危险的科幻世界，在这里，恐怖随时可能向你袭来。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261122/1795311156_751507_jpg_r.jpg
心灵感应能力
你将扮演神秘少女 Elixia，她拥有独特的超能力，这些能力在战斗与解谜中都至关重要。灵活运用各种超能力，在危机中求生并克服重重挑战。你可以释放如子弹般强劲的念力冲击波，利用念力操控物体并将其高速投掷出去，以强大的压力使敌人向内坍缩，还能生成屏障来阻挡敌人的攻击并进行反击。
生存恐怖
体验耳目一新的生存恐怖玩法——本作将资源管理、探索折返与环境解谜等经典生存恐怖元素与动态环境相结合，让你能够随机应变，应对各种危机。
开辟属于你的求生之路——无论是选择正面迎战，还是悄无声息地潜行避敌，一切由你决定。自由探索这座神秘的科幻实验室，与周围环境互动，在步步惊心的探索过程中揭开隐藏的危险与秘密。
追踪者
直面令人毛骨悚然的追猎者——这些由邪恶实验创造出的扭曲怪物各自拥有独特的能力，是一群不达目的誓不罢休的危险猎手，将不惜一切代价追杀你。

content.v: 第一人称动作恐怖游戏《ILL》新宣传片公开，在这款动作恐怖游戏中玩家被困在一座阴森的要塞中，被某个神秘存在所囚禁。难以预知的怪物、真实的肢解系统以及逼真的物理效果，共同营造出无尽的恐怖氛围。游戏将于2027年发售，登陆PC Steam，Xbox Series X|S和PS5，支持中文。
关于这款游戏
《ILL》是一款极致逼真的第一人称生存恐怖游戏，即便是该类型的老玩家也将面临前所未有的挑战。这款游戏将带你坠入阴森诡谲的暗黑世界，充满压迫感的剧情设计让游戏的每一分钟都令人窒息。
开发团队堪称恐怖美学专家，曾与多位知名导演合作，参与过《长脚怪》、《直到黎明》、《致命录像带：超越》、《小丑回魂：欢迎来到德里镇》、《死亡天使》等影视作品的制作。如今，这群造梦者终于要实现夙愿——打造一款能撕裂理智、将你内心最深层的恐惧层层剥开的惊悚杰作。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261122/1795310610_521192_jpg_r.jpg
逼真骇人的恐怖体验
你将深陷一座巨型科研要塞的诡谲阴谋之中，面对神秘邪恶本源及其催生的可怖“异变体”。主角必须冲破重重阻碍，才能拯救心中至珍至重之物。《ILL》将让你身临其境，体验分秒必争的生存之战。
强烈的肉体恐怖和刺骨音效
《ILL》以血腥的真实感突破类型极限：你可以无情肢解那些骇人怪物——撕裂的皮肉、裸露的骨骼、破碎的残躯将震撼你的灵魂，在你的记忆深处打下永恒的烙印。双声道音频系统强化沉浸感，每声惨叫都让你清晰感知痛苦。
动态敌人行为和真实物理效果
游戏中的敌人行为难以预测，而真实的物理效果让游戏世界不仅仅是静态背景，更成为玩法的重要组成部分——包括解谜环节。你的每个动作都可能影响怪物行为：它们会根据环境产生本能反应，并展现出令人毛骨悚然的智能。
战术武器和资源管理
每件武器都通过精细动画展现其独特的物理特性，让你真实感受手中武器的分量。精准射击远远不够——你需仔细检查军火库中每件武器的状态，并进行改装升级。完善的物品管理策略将决定生死存亡，而亲手制作的关键道具甚至可能扭转战局。

一款以传统日式住宅为舞台的第三人称生存恐怖游戏，你将在其中面对神秘的超自然怪异。

items.title: 《艾萨克·戴夫的结合》在创作者回应和评论轰炸后，从《忏悔+》中删除了未公开的人工智能生成的音乐
items.summary: The Binding of Isaac developer Nicalis has removed undisclosed AI-generated music included in Repentance+ afte

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/21/the-binding-of-isaac-repentance-ai-1795303836559.png

The Binding of Isaac developer Nicalis has removed undisclosed AI-generated music included in Repentance+ after backlash led to a review-bombing campaign on Steam and a response from the game's creator, Edmund McMillen.

McMillen and Nicalis spent months building up to the November 19, 2026, release date for the latest update in their classic action roguelike game, but that launch was quickly soured. Just 8% of The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s recent Steam reviews are positive, with a good chunk of comments left by players referencing AI-generated material that was not previously mentioned in any official capacity.
"Thanks, Nicalis, for breaking everything and adding AI slop to an already-existing game!" one popular review said .

"I'm starting to think that adding AI to a game should be valid grounds to refunds to people who have already paid for and played a game," another said . "Shameful they would do this to an Indie gem. Shameful."

The allegedly AI-generated content in question seems to be music exclusively tied to a specific, Grand Theft Auto-themed run meant to coincide with the recent release of GTA 6 . What could have been a cute jab at another gaming titan boiled into a full-blown controversy for Nicalis when Reddit user ShweetsStuff reported the questionable tunes just one day after launch.

As artificial intelligence advances, it's become increasingly difficult to discern human-made art from content pushed out by machines, but ShweetsStuff was able to provide evidence backing their claims. Specifically, they pointed to a handful of tracks that mention AI music software Suno in their metadata, which also included links to their Suno pages.

AI-generated content passed off as art has already become controversial on its own in recent years. Adding to the fire for The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ was the fact that the music was featured in the new update without any sort of update to its Steam description. Valve requires developers to disclose how they may have used AI during game development, making the music's inclusion as puzzling as it is concerning for those who felt Nicalis had pulled the wool over their eyes.

Negative reviews poured in following ShweetsStuff's discovery, leading McMillen to issue a statement today. He said he “had no idea" how AI-generated music found its way into the launch build of The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s new update.
"Woke up to a s**t show," he said , "obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned."
Please report issues and bugs to the email attached.

Just hours later, Nicalis launched a new patch, confirming the "removal of generated music files." The update is currently live for PC, with the studio adding that it has already been submitted to Microsoft, Nintendo, and Sony. When exactly it will go live for those platforms remains to be seen.

No explanation for how or why the AI-generated music was included was provided. Instead, the team simply said it was "working on the game and will continue to address new and old bugs." McMillen also encouraged fans to report issues and bugs to the developers.

In the meantime, The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s recent reviews on Steam remain firmly in the "Overwhelmingly Negative" category. The major update also coincided with the launch of Repentance+ on new platforms, including Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S. For more, you can read IGN's 9/10 review for The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth and our 9/10 review for Afterbirth+ .

items.summary: November 19 marked the highest-traffic day in the ISP's history.

content.v: In a post to X, "The Everything App," US entertainment and communications conglomerate Comcast revealed that Grand Theft Auto 6's historic launch drove record-breaking internet traffic. According to Comcast, only a quarter of "the entire internet" was downloading Rockstar's latest cozy game phenomenon .

"GTA 6 didn't just break records in gaming," Comcast wrote. "Its launch drove the biggest internet traffic day in our network history, with traffic climbing 31% above an average day. At peak, GTA 6 accounted for nearly a quarter of all network traffic."

Comcast shared a video of a line graph showing the massive relative spike in activity on November 19. The chart is unlabeled except for the date, but it presumably corresponds to the volume of data being downloaded across Comcast's entire network.

And that last but does add a caveat to the numbers Comcast cited: Its network and "the entire internet" are two different things, unless I'm missing something here or Comcast's data accounts for other ISPs and other countries, not just its own services.

Regardless, it's still a significant bit of fun with statistics, another example of the totalizing footprint of what may be the largest commercial launch in entertainment history . Imagine how much bigger it would have been launching on PC as well.

items.title: GTA 6 Players Report Crashes on PS5 With Error CE-108255-1
items.summary: GTA 6 players on PlayStation 5 have reported frequent crashes tied to error code CE-108255-1, and it looks lik

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/27/exclusivelookbr-gtfm-1787873244868.png

GTA 6 players on PlayStation 5 have reported frequent crashes tied to error code CE-108255-1, and it looks like it's blocking them from progressing through the story while they wait for Sony and Rockstar to send out a fix.

Although Rockstar Games spent a decade making its new Grand Theft Auto game, it's no surprise to see the new highest-rated game of all time launching with at least a few hiccups. Some have it worse than others, though, with more than a few reports of crashes affecting PS5 consoles popping up online in the days following GTA 6's launch.

The most common cause seems to be tied to error code CE-108255-1, which, as defined by Sony , simply indicates that "an error occurred with the game/application." It seems that, although the majority of players aren't encountering the issue, those who have haven't been able to find a proper fix. Adding to the trouble is that those who have met these dreaded GTA 6 crashes are getting them pretty frequently, and what's triggering them isn't always clear. There are reports from players on both standard PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles running into these issues, with some even saying that crashes appear to be tied to the story, barring them from making any progress.

"I've noticed that the issue manifests differently for different players," one Reddit user said . "In my case, the game crashes on Jason's loading screen: it freezes and then displays the CE-108255-1 error code, meaning I can't even get into the game. Others manage to play for a few minutes before experiencing a crash. I really hope Sony and Rockstar work together to investigate and resolve this issue as soon as possible."

Game crashes are annoying for anyone, but when a massive game like GTA 6, which many feel has a less-than-generous autosave system , suddenly boots players back to the PS5 home screen without warning, it can be especially troublesome. Many who have reported the crashes to PlayStation Support say they've been directed to Rockstar, while those who report to Rockstar say they're being directed to PlayStation. One player said they feel like they're "stuck in an endless support loop, with a game I paid for and still can't play."

Meanwhile, those who have managed to get help say most assistance hasn't been able to completely resolve their issues. However, some have said they've had luck with a few tried-and-true methods, such as uninstalling and reinstalling the game, making sure both the PS5 and game have their most recent updates, and restoring licenses.

"I’ve done everything possible to solve this," another player said . "Deleted cache. Rebuilt database, deleted everything else from my console, took it apart, cleaned it, turned HDR off, switched to 1080p, went and updated game license, deleted and reinstalled and still crashing. Ugh. I’ve got a day 1 PS5 with a disc drive. Other friends of mine with the same console are playing with no issue."
Again, it's unclear if the crashing issue is tied specifically to the PS5 or GTA 6 itself. Until either entity comes up with an update, though, all affected players are stuck on launch weekend.

GTA 6 released for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19 and, in its first 24 hours, made Rockstar $3.79 billion. It's the most successful launch in the history of entertainment , and although its exact unit sales have yet to be disclosed, parent company Take-Two Interactive was at least willing to share that it sold 32.5 million copies in pre-orders alone.

For more, you can read about the players unhappy with how Rockstar handled Jason's secret stash . You can also see the lengths the developers went to in order to create realistic NPCs , as well as the Neuralink user who spent launch driving around Leonida with his mind .

items.title: 育碧“第一个可玩的基于人工智能的研发项目”背后的团队已成立为自己的子公司，名为 Motherbrain
items.summary: In the name of "more immersive and engaging player experiences," of course.

content.v: Use of generative AI in game dev remains as contentious as it does ubiquitous— a recent GDC report found that around 40% of devs use AI, but more than half think its influence has been negative. Ubisoft is continuing to double down on the technology , this time with Motherbrain, a new subsidiary fashioned from the team behind its "first playable generative AI experience."

As reported by VGC , Motherbrain's purpose is to develop "AI for gameplay innovation, supporting all game creators in developing groundbreaking experiences … Its current focus is on new player experiences, smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large scale systemic worlds," according to an earnings report which was released Thursday.

The information comes at a turbulent time for the publishing giant, which just laid off 166 employees even after Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced "outperformed expectations." A sweeping internal overhaul earlier this year saw the company reorganize its workforce into a throng of "creative houses," a decision which led to swathes of layoffs and six project cancellations, including the Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time Remake.

It's not clear what Motherbrain are at work on, in specific terms, right now, but there may be some clues in its past work. That playable AI "experience" I mentioned earlier is none other than Teammates, an R&D project based on a prior experiment with uncanny AI "neo-NPCs."

Teammates aimed to allow players to command NPC squadmates in a rudimentary shooter game with a microphone, and using AI, have those squadmates react believably. It's not far off, at least conceptually, from what we've seen in games like Where Winds Meet and Fortnite , both of which have experimented with AI-powered NPCs.

items.title: 当你在 GTA 6 的保护性监护任务中遇到 Abe 时，你应该继续还是推迟？
items.summary: Should you meet with your lawyer or wait and do it later?

content.v: Deciding whether to proceed or postpone the Protective Custody story mission is a big choice you'll need to make in GTA 6 . The mission appears on your map as "Meet Abe" in Chapter 5, once you've completed the mission Operation Savage Glory.
Once you get to Abe's office, Jason will warn Lucia that everything will change after this mission. Lucia will hesitate at the door as you make your choice to "Proceed" or "Postpone."

This is a pretty big decision, because Protective Custody kicks off the final mission of the game which takes about an hour to play. And even though it's a binary choice between "Proceed" (which starts the mission) and "Postpone" (which delays the mission)" there's actually a third possible outcome based on when you make the choice.
Proceed or Postpone

It's a long mission that will take about an hour to play, so be prepared. You can't save during this mission so make sure you've got the time! Once you've completed the final mission, you can watch the credits and return to the open world so you can continue playing.
You will go back to the open world to continue playing. The "Meet Abe" icon will remain on your map so you can begin the final mission at any point from then on.
The third option:
Proceed with $2 million in your Buck Me savings account

There are multiple endings to GTA 6, and I won't spoil them here. But one of the endings is only possible if you postpone the Protective Custody mission until you've deposited $2 million into your Buck Me savings account . That's why when you choose to proceed with the final mission makes a difference.

It's also worth noting (again, without spoilers) that just because you do have $2 million in your Buck Me savings account does not guarantee you will see this particular ending. There are still choices you'll need to make in the final mission that determine which ending you see.

items.summary: "You can't help but take it a little bit personally".

content.v: When Bethesda got its hands on the Fallout licence way back in 2004, the naysayers were many and vocal. In fairness, the naysayers are still many and vocal, but they were back then too, and it turns out Bethesda saw at least a few of their posts. In a chat with The Examined Game , Skyrim lead Bruce Nesmith reflected on the reaction some Fallout old-heads had to Bethesda's acquisition of the series.

"There was huge pushback when Bethesda got the Fallout licence to do Fallout 3. There was a lot of people who were Obsidian fans, who were like 'Bethesda's gonna screw it up, they're just gonna make it Skyrim, we want Fallout the way we remember Fallout', and there was a strong, vocal community that just hated that we were gonna make that game".

For clarity's sake, the angry fans at the time were likely Black Isle and Interplay fans rather than Obsidian fans—the latter studio hadn't ever made a Fallout game in 2004 (though it had Fallout alumni on staff), and they were prophesying (after 2006) that Bethesda's take on Fallout would be like Oblivion, not Skyrim, since the latter released in 2011. I suspect Nesmith is muddling the initial negative reaction with, well, the more modern one, which is shaped in large part by Obsidian's excellent Fallout: New Vegas from 2010.

"We had to prove them wrong", recalls Nesmith, "and fortunately we did, because Fallout 3 was embraced even by a lot of our sceptics". It's true: people bloody loved Fallout 3 and still do, though there are of course still series fans who reject the game. "There's always going to be some diehard people that say 'Fallout 2 was the greatest Fallout game ever', but we tried our best to just not engage… because you're not going to win that argument.
"All you can do is make the best game you can and let that be your statement. And that's what Bethesda did".

Does the vitriol ever get to Bethesda and its devs? Unsurprisingly, yeah, a little. "Any time somebody says that the thing you're doing is, you know, fill in your blank for all the cuss words and the bad things… you feel like it's a statement about yourself. You have to divorce yourself from that [but] you can't help but take it a little bit personally. But it does make you want to prove them wrong. It does make you want to say 'I'm going to show you that this will work, that we can respect the franchise and make it better and make it our way, rather than the old way".

content.v: The BF Bandito is one of the many cars in GTA 6 that Moses asks you to steal and bring to him for cold, hard cash. This one has a search area out in Buskin Swamp, but when you arrive it's not immediately clear where or how to steal the car.

The owner of this white offroad racer will drive around the map marked search area in a circle, as shown in the clip above. To get him to stop, simply park your car blocking the track and stand next to it. When he reaches you, he'll slow down and call out, at which point you should press L2 to focus on him and use the "Mislead" dialogue option to ask for help.

In my version, Lucia was wearing a ski-mask and had a baseball bat, which quickly convinced them all to run away (after a few swings), but either way, once he stops it's easy to steal the car. The baseball bat probably wasn't necessary, but hey, it's still non-lethal.

As you exit the swamp, you'll get shot at and pursued by a few of his friends, but the BF Bandito is fast enough to outrun them easily. Bring it back to Moses to get $3,400ish as reward, though this may vary based on condition.

items.title: 在俗气的蒂法小玩意的刺激下，上海从不诚实经销商处查获的假玩偶
items.summary: Keeping our streets safe.

content.v: As reported by The Shanghai Observer and Automaton , authorities in Shanghai have arrested 13 people and seized an untold number of unauthorized model kits and figures based on pop culture properties like Final Fantasy. The cops were reportedly put on the trail by a suspect Tifa Lockheart figurine.

Police in Fengxian, a district of Shanghai, began receiving complaints in June. The Shanghai Observer showed pictures comparing a Play Arts Kai (Square Enix's premium figure line) Tifa with a seemingly less articulated counterpart in the same outfit. Reading through machine translation, it sounds like customers in the area bought these figures online expecting the genuine article.

The leader of the operation reportedly commissioned a Guangzhou factory to produce the false Tifa and her ilk. They even sold some figures at higher prices than the genuine article, offering added accessories or features not available in the official product.

I'm of two minds about this, personally: I'm generally pro-kitbashing, selling custom figures, and using proxies in trading card games. In the face of some seriously inflated pricing from official merch lines, bootlegs can often be more enticing than the real deal, particularly if they offer features you can't get from official products⁠—the added customization options from this arrested vendor actually sound weirdly pro-consumer.

But it certainly appears, at least from The Shanghai Observer's reporting, that these suspect figures were being presented as the genuine article to customers. Paired with the increased price vs. official merch, and I find myself soured on the whole operation. It may seem small and silly, but as we endure the Golden Age of Scams, it's weirdly nice to see scammers face some consequences somewhere .

content.v: https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/PgGhmt5pTtxusaQQX3dHPF-1920-80.png

This is Terminally Online : PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about their MMO of choice.

World of Warcraft: Foreve r's done a lot of things for me over the past couple of weeks—it's given me a deeper appreciation for oldschool MMO quest design, it's wowed me with some genuinely impressive new lighting technology, and it's… ugh, it's made me so friendly.

Mind, I wouldn't say I'm unkind when I play MMOs, but I am a solo player by habit. I'll have a guild, friends I roleplay with, sure. But I'm very rarely striking up conversations with people in-game—all of that typically happens in Discord. And yet, here I am in WoW forever, trying to emphatically start conversations with goddamn everyone I meet.

And it's in part because of how much of a bastard the game is. I don't think Classic is a particularly difficult videogame—I've even gotten my warrior from level 1 to, at the time of writing, 56 as fury, a spec typically considered trash for levelling. And it's been fine, I've just minded my pulls and levelled first aid.

But it is a known fact that vanilla WoW quests are just easier when you group up with people. Part of this is because players are a force multiplier—many classes have group buffs, and not having to worry about health with a healer present means that you can pull swathes of enemies and melt them down easily.
And so I've been doing that. I've been grouping with people, and they've been grouping with me, and… oh, god, we've been talking to each other .

I don't know if I just happen to have a lucky propensity for drawing in nice folks, but my levelling journey has been dappled with some of the chillest people you'll ever meet. People hanging around to help you finish quests they've already completed is so common it's almost standard.

In one instance, a shadow priest carried me through multiple elite quests in Stranglethorn Vale—they needed to do 'em too, sure, but they actively went out of their way to show me where I could get a couple.

There is a real, tangible sense of camaraderie in the game right now, one that's yet to be grinded to the marrow by the efficiency-laden tasks of Mythic+ or a seasonal system. But it's also one borne of how long everything takes. When you've already spent 10 minutes jogging to a quest, what's another five to help a stranger out?

It is, to put it plainly, the opposite of what I'd expected after years of playing far more modern MMOs. I'm even way ahead of the curve of the general population level-wise, and I'm still meeting these relaxed, generous folks. People who'll offer up scraps of a treasure map that's dropping from the pirates we're grinding for free, rather than being a mercenary about it and selling them on the auction house.

Moreover, it is infectious. I've been handing mana potions to people. I've been sticking around to help out with quests—in a recent Zul'farrak run, a dungeon I was only doing twice because I'd missed that it was required for the Sunken Temple questline, our tank had simply atrocious luck collecting troll tempers for a quest (you need 20 of them, and they don't drop often).

Not just myself, but another player in the same situation all stuck around for about 20 minutes just to help them out. When they thanked us, I, saccharine and glowing with the spirit of a reformed Grinch, said: "No worries, bud, if you wanna live in a village you've gotta be a villager sometimes."
Ugh.

In short, Forever's turned me into a big, fluffy, golden-haired dog. The kind you meet in a park that bounds up to you with its stupid tongue wagging out. All that oldschool game design and camaraderie has, as it turns out, been a complete antidote to my hermetic ways. And while my street cred as a tough, solemn badass might never recover, I'm glad to be taking my time.

content.v: Chapter 2 of GTA 6 finally gives you full control over both Jason and Lucia, and one of the first missions you'll undertake as a criminal couple involves committing a robbery in one of three locations.

One of your options is Avery Pawn Shop, where you'll be able to make a tidy sum of money if you can smash-and-grab enough loot and, more crucially, find the safe code to crack it open for additional cash and jewellery.The easiest way to do that is to grab the code for the safe, which is thankfully pretty easy to do.
How to find the Avery Pawn Shop safe code

items.title: GTA 6 中最不可饶恕的罪行是电视植入
items.summary: Jason and Cal do their best to redecorate the bach' pad but c'mon boys, a TV in front of a giant glass door? W

content.v: Grand Theft Auto 6 is a game about criminals doing crimes. Car crimes, gun crimes, drug crimes, and first degree decorating crimes. Early in the game, Jason's buddy Cal convinces him that he's got to turn his r/malelivingspace shack into a place he can bring his girl Lucia without feeling like she's still stuck in a jail cell. Cal is right, but his decorating decisions should be illegal.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/gzE7aecf5nV2nHJWnbqkE3-1920-80.jpg

This is how Jason's living room looks at the beginning of the game while he's still flying solo. Not great, Jason. If I've learned anything from lurking in interior decorating communities online it's that furniture should never be touching your walls, no matter how small the room is, and that nobody's TV is ever at the right height.

Cal hassles Jason into moving some things around and, while I love his motivation, he makes everything worse. What they wind up with is this: couch blocking prime navigation space and the TV sitting in front of the sliding glass door. Look, I know the point is that Cal is an incompetent dork. He's slugging beers and insisting they make the room feng shui. I can't forgive him for this one though.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/wkzxjwEVk58pEhkE4Gj7i5-1920-80.png

Cal does get one thing right here: using the couch and arm chair to create a space that feels like a living room within the open area. Once Lucia moves in she and Jason continue making the waterfront shack more homey. They get a rug in the living room, a classic choice to finish tying that space into a room. Lucia brings home a coffee table to assemble (cute domestic conversation ensues). The dining table gets centered properly in its corner.

But that damn TV stays parked in front of the glass door. It's criminal! There would be so much glare on that screen from the east and west facing windows and light all day long drowning it out from behind that north facing glass door. My sad, myopic eyes are tearing up just thinking about squinting at it.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/yxKJDH7N43yUKFB9Got66C-1920-80.png

So I took Jason's conundrum to one of the interior decorating communities on Reddit to ask for some group workshopping. They immediately grasped the unforgivable TV placement and the inherent issue with the number of windows in this place. Almost no wall is safe here.

One suggestion was to keep those window blinds in the living room down and place the TV stand in front of it. Makes sense to me—Jason wouldn't be losing much light with all the other windows in here. Another more minor fix was to just put the TV at a 45 degree angle in its corner so it's less directly in front of the glass door, though I don't think that solves the glare problems.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/RtZM2xtic2sHFmNFkjwYL5-1920-80.png

The more popular suggestion (and my favorite) was to swap the dining and living room. The TV can sit on the rear wall, slightly tucked away with the blinds pulled down, while the dining table gets easier access from the kitchen and doesn't suffer for being lit from all sides.

Alas, I have it on good authority that the TV never manages to move from where Cal stuck it. I can forgive drug smuggling, but I draw the line at suboptimal viewing angles. Ah well, perhaps Jason and Lucia have a better floor plan to work with in the next place they move to as their criminal exploits grow.

items.title: 当我还是个孩子的时候，我的阁楼里没有怪物，我有一个局域网
items.summary: I'm not boasting. OK, I am a bit.

content.v: Weird Weekend is our regular Saturday column where we celebrate PC gaming oddities: peculiar games, strange bits of trivia, forgotten history. Pop back every weekend to find out what Jeremy, Josh, Rick and Ted have become obsessed with this time, whether it's the canon height of Thief's Garrett or that time someone in the Vatican pirated Football Manager .

Multiplayer gaming on PC these days is so easy you probably barely even think about it. Most games that support multiplayer will work out of the gate, and there's an abundance of ways to connect and chat with your friends across the globe. This is a far cry from the early days of PC multiplayer, when dial-up connections and ad-hoc servers made multiplayer PC gaming expensive and unreliable.

Indeed, the best way to play multiplayer PC games back then was via a LAN. A local network offered the fastest and most stable connections, and didn't cost you anything beyond the hardware required to hook it all together. Unfortunately, it was also the least convenient way of playing PC games with your friends, as it meant one or several of you had to haul your whole-ass PC to an agreed-upon location.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/bbcM2WRFpDZoBw2LKtfzM9-1920-80.jpg

Because of this, LAN gaming was a rare treat for most people in the '90s and early '00s. Unless, that is, you happened to be a disgustingly lucky bastard like myself, and had a LAN in your attic that you could play at any time.

Now, this sounds like the kind of lie a 10-year-old would blurt out in the playground to impress his friends (specifically, an eight-year-old from the mid '90s who had a working knowledge of PC gaming, which, I concede, is a limited demographic) and indeed, the further away I get from that time, the more like a false memory it seems. But it is 100% true, and I have the pictures to prove it.

The LAN (as it was simply and practically known) was in service between 2001 and 2003, and existed because of my family's long-running enthusiasm for PCs and PC gaming. As I've mentioned in other articles, my dad was fascinated by the internet from 1994 onward, both just as a technology and for the business opportunities it offered. Meanwhile, his brother (my uncle) was an IT support expert and a dedicated PC gamer.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ifKH2PSFssqAvB8bWtPzo8-1920-80.jpg

Since they were close as siblings and shared this mutual interest (at least on the PC aspect—my dad was never much of a gamer) there was a constant stream of PC hardware flowing through the house, as they tried to keep up with the rapid progress of PCs through the '90s. Eventually, when they'd upgrade a PC, they began taking the old components and building them into a "new" PCs. This is how my brother and I ended with our joint PC in 1997, and how we ended up with individual PCs a few years later.

In 2000 my family (and, separately, my uncle) moved to the Isle of Man, which for non UK audiences is a small island between Britain and Ireland known for two things: tail-less cats and incredibly dangerous motorbike races. The house we rented there had a converted attic—complete with creaky, bare-floorboard stairs—and my dad decided this was the ideal space to set up all three PCs.

Initially the PCs weren't connected. But the layout of the room meant it was only a matter of time before my dad and uncle had that particular brainwave. At some point in 2001, another upgrade happened, and we were left with spare parts for a fourth PC, which could be used as a dedicated server to network the other three PCs together.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/TaaKeAqk63bpsjniJrGJM9-1920-80.jpg

The upshot was we had a three-PC LAN on which we could play multiplayer games. I have a distinct memory of them clunking about in the attic while setting this up—likely over a weekend or possibly that year's Easter holiday. I also remember them showing it to us once they were done and explaining how it all worked.

What I don't remember, annoyingly, is what the first game we played on it was. It might have been Doom, though I can't say for certain. I think the reason I don't remember is that once the LAN was set up, my brother and I were largely left to our own devices to get games running on it. Hence, a lot of my memories surrounding the LAN are about that , rather than the games we actually played.

Even with the hard work of setting up the LAN done, getting games to work on it often proved a challenge. Since each PC was the product of multiple rounds of leftovers, they all had different components, so the chance of encountering compatibility issues with a game on at least one of the PCs was not insignificant. The difference between a 1998 PC and a 2001 PC was cavernous, so they might have a processor that was too old, a graphics card that didn't support the latest DirectX, insufficient RAM.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/kxJK6RFASfAMXQewNLkRy8-1920-80.jpg

In addition, while we had three PCs, we'd typically only have one copy of any given game, which meant rolling the dice on copy protection with every game we tried (and occasionally searching the murkier corners of the Internet for a crack or a keygen— don't tell the police .) Even if the game installed successfully, there would often be a question of whether it could find the dedicated server on each PC, or whether I'd have to go futzing around in the network settings—not an easy thing to do when you're 13 and stupid.

Nonetheless, there were quite a few games that made it all the way through the gauntlet. The one I remember most vividly is Half-Life: Opposing Force deathmatch—which was basically Half-Life deathmatch with more maps and more weapons. One of OpFor's multiplayer maps, Datacore , was the perfect size for three players, and we'd spend hours setting up laser traps for one another around the map's tight, electric-blue corridors. Another favourite was Paradox Park , which we spent ages in despite the fact it was impractically large for three players.

Pragmatism influenced what we played a lot. While my brother and I never struggled to fill that third chair (weirdly, it isn't hard to get other kids to come around to your house when you have a LAN in your attic), three players was a challenging number with a lot of games, so we tended to play stuff that had a small-scale deathmatch. That said, we definitely attempted some lopsided rounds of Counter-Strike , each taking it in turns to be the odd one out. Any game with bots, like Unreal Tournament , we considered sacred.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/6BEY7RjbgyfvfWB6b3Kri8-1920-80.jpg

Some of the stuff we played was just weird . There was a Half-Life mod called Firearms , which just had a shitload of guns in it, that we sank hours into. At one point I got super into Operation Flashpoint's map editor, and—influenced by watching Enemy at the Gates—created multiplayer sniper duels where two or three players would play lethal hide and seek in one of its various low-poly towns. When there wasn't a third player available, my brother and I would spend hours hacking each other to bits in Severance: Blade of Darkness' multiplayer duel mode. Did you know that Severance: Blade of Darkness had a multiplayer duel mode? We certainly did, and I think we probably played it more than anybody else.

Looking back, it's wild how hacky the whole experience was. Not the LAN itself—that always worked fine. But how our requirements versus the limitations of what was available affected what we played. Our siloed, odd-numbered setup was perfectly suited for the kind of modern, cooperative gaming experience that did not exist at all back then. But in some ways that was part of the magic. Any new game we got, we'd check the back of the box to see if it had a multiplayer mode and how many players it supported. If we could install and run it on all three PCs and see the host server, holy shit, that was almost as thrilling as playing the game itself.
